groups.intro:
Whether and how the state credentials this profession — the regulatory model,
credential type, issuing authority, entry requirements (education, exams, age,
character), fees, renewal, continuing education, and reciprocity.

fields.meaning: Whether the state requires a credential to practice this profession.

example.quote: The board shall issue a license to engage in the practice of public accounting to an individual who meets the requirements of AS 08.04.110 - 08.04.130.

fields.meaning: Free-text name of the board/agency that issues the credential (the structured form is `regulatory_authority`).

example.quote: There is created the Board of Public Accountancy.

fields.meaning: Structured decomposition of the issuing authority — name, type (standalone board / shared board / division / department / joint), and any umbrella agency it sits within. Populated alongside the legacy free-text issuing_authority for back-compat.
Canonical name of the immediate authority (e.g., 'State Board of Podiatry').

example.quote: There is created the Board of Public Accountancy.

fields.meaning: Structural classification of the immediate authority.

example.quote: There is created the Board of Public Accountancy.

fields.meaning: Higher-level agency that contains the immediate authority, if any. Example: 'Division of Occupations and Professions, Department of Commerce'. Null for standalone boards that don't sit inside a larger department.

example.value: Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development
example.quote: "department" means the Department of Commerce, Community, and Economic Development

fields.meaning: Minimum age (years) to hold the credential, if the statute sets one.
Whether the statute conditions licensure on good moral character / fitness.

example.quote: An applicant for a certified public accountant license shall be of good moral character.

fields.meaning: Education entry requirement — degree, level, accreditation, and any tiers.

example.value: baccalaureate degree or its equivalent conferred by a college or university acceptable to the board and additional semester hours or post-baccalaureate study so that the total educational program includes at least 150 hours

fields.meaning: How the statute decides a school counts. national_accreditor=a named national program accreditor (ACOE/CODA/ACEND/LCME/CPME). regional_accreditor='regionally accredited college or university'. board_approved='approved by the board' (discretionary state gate). unspecified=says 'accredited' with no basis named, or silent.

example.quote: a baccalaureate degree or its equivalent conferred by a college or university acceptable to the board

fields.meaning: True if the statute pegs the education requirement to a NATIONAL CREDENTIAL (e.g. 'registered by CDR', 'passed the NBEO') rather than (or in addition to) a stated degree — such a state inherits whatever that national body currently requires.

fields.meaning: Per-tier floors when the statute sets different education levels for different license classes, or phases the floor in by date. Omit/null when there is a single floor. `degree_level` still records the overall floor across all tiers.
Which class/date this floor applies to — e.g. 'licensed dietitian', 'certified nutritionist', 'applicants on or after 2024-01-01'.

Normalized education floor, low -> high. Resolved to the rung even when
the statute uses verbiage ('six college years' -> doctorate, 'or equivalent
degree' -> the named level). Professional/clinical doctorates (OD, DDS, MD,
DPM) are `doctorate`.
ISO date when this floor takes effect, for date-phased tiers (e.g. '2024-01-01'). Null otherwise.
Supervised practice / residency / apprenticeship required after the degree.

example.quote: two years of accounting experience satisfactory to the board

fields.meaning: ALWAYS populate (required_by_statute / embedded_in_credential / none) unless the governing statute is absent from the corpus. Disambiguates a blank `required`: 'none' (truly no requirement) vs 'embedded_in_credential' (the accredited degree the statute points to carries the supervised hours).

example.quote: two years of accounting experience satisfactory to the board

fields.meaning: e.g. '24 months', '1 year', '2,000 hours' (free text — units vary)

fields.meaning: e.g. 'podiatric residency', 'accounting work experience', 'AXP'

fields.meaning: Examinations required for the credential (one entry per exam).

example.value: Administered by the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants; board uses AICPA's advisory grading service if available.

fields.meaning: Where the exam is administered / who owns it — e.g. 'NBPME (national)', 'state board (in-state)', 'NCLEX-RN (national)'. Use the statute's language; null if the source doesn't say.
Max attempts allowed before re-qualification. Null if not specified.
How the credential is renewed — interval and any conditions.
Most states are 1 or 2

example.quote: Licenses shall be renewed biennially on the dates set by the department with the approval of the respective board.

fields.meaning: License renewal fee in US dollars (integer). Many statutes leave the amount to the board's discretion — leave null in that case.
Continuing-education requirement to keep the credential active.

during the two years immediately preceding the application

fields.meaning: Specific topical CE requirements, e.g. ['1.5 hrs opioid', 'ethics']
Whether/how the state recognizes out-of-state credentials (endorsement/reciprocity).

example.quote: the board may issue a license to engage in the practice of public accounting to an applicant who holds a license, or its equivalent, issued by another state

fields.meaning: Free-form summary

example.value: Applicant must have passed the Uniform CPA Examination, meet board-established accounting experience requirements, not be subject to pending disciplinary proceedings in another state, and be of good moral character.
example.quote: passed the Uniform Certified Public Accountant Examination of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants in order to receive the applicant's initial license from the other state; meets the

fields.meaning: Profession-specific advisory body sitting alongside the main licensing board, when one exists. Populated for states that delegate licensure to a generic board and add a specialty advisory committee.
True if a profession-specific advisory body exists alongside the main licensing board. False if the licensing board itself is profession-specific (no separate advisory body needed).

example.quote: There is created the Board of Public Accountancy.

fields.meaning: Name of the advisory board, e.g. 'Podiatry Advisory Committee'.
Authority the advisory board has, in the statute's own words — e.g. 'advisory only', 'rulemaking subject to board approval', 'disciplinary recommendations'. Free text from the statute.

Name of a national CERTIFICATION the state recognizes or requires, e.g. 'American Board of Podiatric Surgery (ABPS)' or 'National Board of Podiatric Medical Examiners (NBPME)'. The certifying body, NOT the association. Null if the statute doesn't reference one.

Professional ASSOCIATION the state references (e.g. for accreditation or CE provider approval) — 'American Podiatric Medical Association (APMA)', 'American Dental Association (ADA)'. Distinct from the certifying body. Null if not referenced.

example.value: American Institute of Certified Public Accountants
example.quote: The board shall use the Uniform Certified Public Accountant Examination of the American Institute of Certified Public Accountants and the institute's advisory grading service, if available.

fields.meaning: Which UORF model the state applies to this profession (license / mandatory_cert / registration / etc).

example.quote: The board shall issue a license to engage in the practice of public accounting to an individual who meets the requirements of AS 08.04.110 - 08.04.130.

fields.meaning: What SHAPE of credential does the state issue, independent of whether holding it is mandatory? license / certification / registration / exemption / none. Pairs with is_mandatory to decompose the legacy regulatory_model rung.

example.quote: The board shall issue a license to engage in the practice of public accounting to an individual who meets the requirements of AS 08.04.110 - 08.04.130.

fields.meaning: Is the credential MANDATORY to practice (or claim the title) in this state? True if practicing without it is prohibited; False if optional (e.g., voluntary certification that only protects the title for those who hold it).

example.quote: Only a person who holds a valid license, practice privilege, or permit may issue a report on behalf of another person or governmental unit.

fields.meaning: Does the state restrict use of the profession's title to licensees? True if unlicensed people may NOT call themselves the protected title (e.g. 'podiatrist', 'CPA').

example.quote: An individual may not assume or use the title or designation "certified public accountant" or the abbreviation "CPA" or any other title, designation, word, letter, abbreviation, sign, card, or device

fields.meaning: Does the state restrict practice of the profession's scope to licensees? True if performing the scope without a license is prohibited (independent of title use).

example.quote: Only a person who holds a valid license, practice privilege, or permit may issue a report on behalf of another person or governmental unit.

fields.meaning: Grounds on which the board may discipline a licensee. Typical statutes list 5-15.
snake_case key, e.g. 'fraud_in_obtaining_license'
One-line plain-English description

example.value: Fraud or deceit in obtaining a license or permit required by this chapter.

fields.meaning: Non-credential regulatory mechanisms (bonding, insurance, establishment regulation) imposed by the state. Obama 2015 framework typology. Independent of credential_type.
Does the statute require the practitioner or firm to post a bond (funds against which consumer claims can be made)? Independent of whether a credential is also required.
Does the statute require the practitioner or firm to carry insurance (e.g., professional liability, surety insurance)?
Does the statute regulate the ESTABLISHMENT / FIRM (e.g., facility license, mandatory inspection of premises) as a route to consumer protection, independent of any practitioner credential?

example.quote: Each office established or maintained in this state for the practice of public accounting shall be under the direct supervision of an individual who holds a license issued under this chapter.

fields.meaning: Statutory citations supporting the licensure fields above.

groups.intro:
What the practice act lets (or reserves to) this profession — the defined scope,
authorized methods, drug authority, and any title/scope protection. Skeleton only —
profession-specific scope richness lives in the discovered block.

fields.meaning: Verbatim statutory definition; quote field repeats the value text.

example.quote: "compilation service" means a service of any compilation engagement performed in accordance with the Statements on Standards for Accounting and Review Services

Whether a separate ethics examination (e.g., AICPA ethics exam or state-specific ethics exam) is required as a condition of initial licensure.
Whether out-of-state CPAs with substantially equivalent qualifications may practice in the state without providing notice, paying a fee, or making any submission to the board.

fields.meaning: Whether individuals with practice privileges or individual licensees must perform certain attest services (audits, PCAOB engagements) only through a firm holding a valid permit.

example.quote: An individual licensed under AS 08.04.105 may not perform attest functions through a firm unless the firm holds a valid permit issued under AS 08.04.240.

fields.meaning: Whether a simple majority (more than 50%) of firm ownership in terms of financial interests and voting rights must belong to licensed CPAs.

example.quote: more than one-half of the ownership of the firm belongs to certified public accountants of this or another state in good standing

fields.meaning: Whether CPA firms may include owners who are not licensed CPAs, subject to specified conditions.

fields.meaning: Whether peer review is required as a condition for renewal of a firm permit or registration.

example.quote: The board shall, not more frequently than once every three years, require as a condition for renewal of a permit of a firm that the applicant firm undergo a peer review conducted as required by the bo

fields.meaning: Maximum frequency (in years) at which peer review may be required for firm permit renewal.

example.quote: not more frequently than once every three years, require as a condition for renewal of a permit of a firm that the applicant firm undergo a peer review

fields.meaning: Whether peer review proceedings, records, and work papers are privileged and not subject to discovery or introduction into evidence in civil or administrative proceedings.

example.quote: a peer review be performed and the documents be maintained in a manner that is designed to preserve confidentiality

fields.meaning: Whether a licensee who is not engaged in the practice of public accounting may place their license on inactive status, typically with reduced fees and no CPE requirement.

fields.meaning: Whether a licensee may place their license on a retired status, typically with reduced or no fees and no CPE requirement, with restrictions on active practice.
Whether a firm without an office in the state may provide certain services (compilation, review, or non-attest services) without obtaining a firm permit, subject to specified conditions.

example.quote: The board shall grant a permit to engage in the practice of public accounting to a firm that does not have an office in the state but provides, or offers to provide, attest functions in the state

fields.meaning: Whether each office of a firm established in the state for the practice of public accounting must be under the direct supervision of a licensed CPA.

example.quote: Each office established or maintained in this state for the practice of public accounting shall be under the direct supervision of an individual who holds a license issued under this chapter.

fields.meaning: Whether individuals who sign or authorize signing of attest or compilation reports on behalf of a firm must meet specific competency requirements set out in professional standards.

Whether a licensee is prohibited from performing services for a contingent fee when also performing attest or compilation services for the same client, or from preparing tax returns for a contingent fee.

Whether the statute provides specific safe harbor disclaimer language that nonlicensees may use when preparing financial statements without expressing assurance, thereby avoiding unlicensed practice violations.

example.quote: evidence of the commission of a single act prohibited by this chapter is sufficient to justify an injunction or a conviction without evidence of a general course of conduct

fields.meaning: Whether firms that fall out of compliance with ownership requirements due to changes in personnel are granted a reasonable period to take corrective action before facing permit suspension or revocation.

fields.meaning: Whether a firm must hold a valid permit or registration to provide attest or compilation services, separate from individual licensure requirements.

example.quote: An individual licensed under AS 08.04.105 may not perform attest functions through a firm unless the firm holds a valid permit issued under AS 08.04.240.

fields.meaning: Whether the state has a specialized 'Registered Municipal Accountant' designation requiring additional examination, limited to auditing municipal or county financial statements.
Whether the state has a specialized 'Public School Accountant' designation required for auditing school district financial statements.
Whether the state has a separate 'Accounting Practitioner' or 'Licensed Public Accountant' tier below CPA with its own examination, education, and scope-of-practice requirements.
Whether the state provides a formal 'CPA Emeritus' or 'CPA Retired' status for licensees who have permanently ceased practice, with reduced or no fees and no CPE requirement.
Whether the state imposes additional or specific continuing professional education requirements for CPAs engaged in auditing governmental entities.
Minimum hours of ethics-related continuing professional education required per renewal period.
Whether Hawaii requires a state-specific supplemental peer review report covering Hawaii attest engagements when the primary peer review does not include Hawaii offices or engagements.
Whether the state limits CPA liability to third parties not in privity of contract, with exceptions for fraud, intentional misrepresentation, or known intended reliance.
Specific statute of limitations period for actions based on negligence or breach of contract against accountants, typically shorter than general tort limitations.
Whether the statute explicitly requires a CPA to be independent with respect to an enterprise before expressing an opinion on its financial statements.
Whether the statute explicitly requires a licensee to return client-provided records and furnish copies of working papers that constitute part of the client's records upon client request.
